To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we determined x-ray structures of intact Escherichicola coli ribosome, apo and with one or two tRNAs bound, and that these structures reveal the molecular basis of ratcheting and swiveling during protein synthesis.

x-ray structures of intact Escherichiacoli 70S ribosomes reveal intermediates in the process of intersubunit ratcheting that occur as tRNA molecules move into the hybrid-state of binding that precedesthe final steps of mRNA translocation.

we have determined x-ray crystal structures that reveal intermediate states along the ratchetting pathway of the E. coli ribosome, and that these structures reveal how the head domain of small subunit is positioned by contacts with both large subunit and tRNA in the peptidylyl-tRNA site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the translation elongation cycle.
the molecular mechanisms underlying protein biosynthesis.
the structural and functional analysis of ribosomes and their complexes with antibiotics and translation factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structures of the intact ribosome in the apo form and with one or two tRNA mimics show that the interface between the subunits rearranges during ratcheting in discrete steps.

the structures of the ribosome in intermediate states of ratcheting provide insight into how intersubunit contacts rearrange in discrete steps to facilitate protein synthesis, and how tRNAs are positioned to move from the peptidly-tRNA to the exit-tRNA site.
the structures provide insight into the mechanism of ratcheting and how tRNAs are moved from one site to another on the ribosome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structures reveal how the interface between large and small ribosomal subunits reorients in a discrete fashion during intersubunit ratcheting.
we have solved the structure of the intact ribosome in three different intermediate states of ratcheting.
we have determined the structures of the intact ribosome, in the apo-form or with one or with two anticodon stem loops bound, which represent intermediate states of ratcheting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ribosome can adopt multiple states during ratcheting.

the ratcheting process can be described as a series of discrete steps, with the ribosome in the apo state corresponding to a state in which the large subunit has rotated relative to the small subunit by about 6°.
the ratcheting process is a stepwise process, and that the ribosome can accommodate a range of tRNA conformations during the course of ratcheting.
